name: Versailles
ground: Flat, marshy, and with no strategic value whatsoever, which was the point: nothing about the site constrains the plan, so the plan is purely an argument.

keep.name: The Corps de Logis
keep.note: No keep. There is nothing to defend against, and saying so is the message.

wards.name: Cour de Marbre
wards.note: The narrowest point, so that arriving feels like a funnel.

wards.name: Corps de Logis
wards.note: The block the whole axis runs through.

wards.name: Parterre d’Eau
wards.note: Water, held flat, so the sky is doubled and the axis keeps going.

axis.name: The Grand Axis
axis.note: East to west, so the sun sets along it. That is not a coincidence and it was the single most expensive decision.

gallery.name: Hall of Mirrors
gallery.note: Seventeen mirrored arches facing seventeen windows. The mirrors are there to put the garden on the wall that has no garden behind it.

figures.value: 73 m long, 10.5 m wide, 12.3 m high
exactly 21 — the division is why the room reads calm
the hall is about 7 times as long as it is wide

lesson: One axis, laid out at once, and everything placed to be seen from a point on it. The opposite of Windsor in every way, and equally correct — which is the whole reason both are here. A base is either arrived at or argued, and you should know which one you are doing.
